visualReview.notes: Inspected the site preview, 4 turntables and named views of the historic north clock, west paired portals, structural vaulted nave and polygonal apse. The repaired connecting volumes ground the clock tower and west gable. The interior shows the length and span of the vaults; small upper joins and carved details are simplified.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected 9 dated runtime images. The bounded placement loads the native cathedral and enclosure walls with the shared limestone, roofing, iron and wood bindings. The fixture unloads cleanly. The original terrain was checked separately.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 25 context and detail images. Skyline and district retain both fronts, the clock tower, main nave and polygonal apse. Near levels retain open arch effects, carved-stone forms, grilles, buttresses and the seven-bay three-nave rib vault.

geographicReview.notes: The surveyed cathedral walls use the exact 8-point mapped footprint and both yard enclosures. The west contact is sampled outside the front. I inspected the original unmasked Terrarium field and the terrain-backed preview. Exact historical grade and the north portal axis are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The late nineteenth-century Cathedral of Santo Domingo, with its stone north entrance, clock and bell stage, long Gothic nave, lower chapel roofs and the west front.
fidelityReview.notes: The primary architectural study fixes seven bays, the 45.8 m nave, the 54.6 m entrance-to-presbytery length, the 9.63 m center nave, 4.80 m aisles and stepped chapel roof massing. The Qualla photograph captures the oldest documented clock stage and temple frontage. The March 1915 plate corroborates the retained twin-door and arch-window west front. Carved designs and roof profiles are simplified.

imageryReview.notes: Matched the exact Qualla native JPG to the original 1899 Munsey’s New York periodical. Examined the dated cover and the west photographic plate of the original 1915 Bulletin of the Pan American Union. Both sources are public domain. Later share-alike images, modern stained glass and unverified historical copies were excluded.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Cathedral of Santo Domingo as represented in February 1899, including the original north clock tower, Renaissance west front, vaulted structural naves, chapels, apse and adjacent enclosure walls.

limitations: The preserved mapped enclosure controls the outer shape. The 1899 appearance uses the Qualla north photograph, with the surviving west front corroborated by a published 1915 photograph.
The historic clock tower, external chapel roof pitches, exact portal locations and floor heights are approximate. The nineteenth-century clock mechanism is simplified.
Interior geometry depicts the load-bearing nave, aisles and ribbed vaults with simplified chapel partitions. Furnishings, tombs, stained-glass art and carved relief figures are outside the model.
The original modern elevation source remains unchanged and is used as an estimate for the historical grade.
